claim: Finite-thickness spherical load-relaxation analysis can recover reasonable viscoelastic elasticity where purely elastic models fail, but anisotropy and nonunique or unstable multi-exponential parameter fitting limit direct use of a full generalized-Maxwell state online.
epistemic_status: Formulation, validation, experiments, and fitting limitations are author-reported; online-control implications are bounded inferences.
problem_and_setting: Estimating soft-material elasticity when finite ramp duration, force relaxation, and finite sample thickness invalidate instantaneous infinite-half-space elastic indentation assumptions.
method_or_mechanism: A constant-speed spherical indentation ramp is followed by a position hold. Multi-exponential relaxation maps to a three-branch generalized Maxwell model, with finite-ramp and finite-thickness corrections under near-incompressible, bonded, small-indentation conditions.
content_summary: Finite-element validation and gelatin/chicken-breast experiments show thickness correction matters below roughly ten indenter radii and finite load-relaxation estimates outperform elastic models on chicken breast. Anisotropy and viscosity remain difficult; nonlinear fitting is initialization-sensitive and nonunique, while fixing time constants can yield nonphysical coefficients.
synthesis_role: Evidence for measurable contact memory and finite-thickness effects, coupled with a warning that full relaxation parameters may not be identifiable enough for online control.
development_link: Test a complexity ladder from calibrated memoryless contact to low-order relaxation state, and require extra state to change impedance actions or held-out force/deformation/safety outcomes under ordinary scanning excitation.

evidence.finding: The ramp-hold test models multi-exponential relaxation as a three-branch generalized Maxwell response with ramp/thickness corrections.
Finite-element analysis validates the formulation under its constitutive and geometric assumptions.
Gelatin and chicken-breast estimates agree reasonably with surface-wave comparisons; elastic models fail on viscoelastic chicken breast.
Thickness effects matter below about ten radii; anisotropy and viscosity estimation remain unresolved.
Multi-exponential fitting is nonunique and initialization-sensitive; fixed time constants can produce negative coefficients.

boundary_conditions: Small indentation and constant 0.1 mm/s ramp.
No broad in-vivo tissue diversity or anisotropy.
assumptions: Material properties remain stable during a test.

reported: Elastic models fail on viscoelastic chicken breast.
Anisotropy and direct viscosity estimation are unresolved.
Multi-exponential fitting can be nonunique or nonphysical.
inferred: A memoryless law can miss history-dependent force when relaxation overlaps the task timescale.
The full Maxwell parameter vector may be unsuitable online.
Ramp-hold observability may not transfer to uninterrupted sliding.

conflicts_with: Any purely elastic treatment of relaxing tissue.
Any infinite-half-space assumption for modest thickness.
Any direct adoption of a full generalized-Maxwell vector without identifiability tests.
Any claim that this material test proves improved scanning control.
